facts.text: Safford sprang to life in 1874 when founders Bailey, Kennedy and Tuttle, fleeing flood‑damaged canals, laid out the town after leaving Gila Bend.
The city takes its name from Arizona Territorial Governor Anson P., honoring his early 20th‑century leadership.
Graham International Observatory houses a 20‑inch telescope, the world’s largest permanent mount camera obscura, and a Milky Way shuttle simulator.
The Safford City‑Graham County Library offers free books, computers, and childhood literacy programs to residents.
Southwest of town, the Pinaleño Mountains rise dramatically, boasting the greatest vertical relief of any Arizona range.
Safford’s hot semi‑arid climate sees July highs near 98°F, matching Phoenix’s summer heat despite its lower elevation.
